features.headline: Cowboys need to break a year-long trend to make the playoffs
features.desc: If Dallas is going to catch up to New York in the division, it needs to start stringing wins together.
body: FRISCO, Texas — If anything, the Dallas Cowboys' 51-30 win against the Tennessee Titans kept them afloat with six games to play.

At 5-6, the Cowboys will need the NFC East—leading New York Giants (6-3-1) to lose some games if they want to win the division, but in the minutes after the Tennessee victory, owner and general manager Jerry Jones spoke optimistically about what his team had just done.
Fifty-one points. Six different players scored a touchdown. Only three first-half field goals for the Titans. Five sacks for the defense.
"It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we want to do," Jones said.
Hope, however, can be a week-to-week thing. And in this case, maybe even shorter than that considering the Cowboys play NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving (4:30 p.m. ET, Fox).
The Cowboys are not out of the NFC East race, but they're not exactly in it either. To get there, they have to keep winning, and a year has passed since they last posted consecutive wins.
Last Thanksgiving, the Cowboys beat the Kansas City Chiefs for their third straight win to improve to 6-5-1. They won only one game the rest of the way.
This season, the Cowboys had four other opportunities to post back-to-back wins and came up short. Going one step forward and one step back has kept the Cowboys mired in mediocrity.
Coaches and players have been asked so often about whether they can string together wins that they can only go to gallows humor.
"When the clock says zero, we have to have more points than the other team," coach Brian Schottenheimer said.

features.headline: Commanders building momentum, halt Bengals' 5-game win streak
features.desc: The Commanders' defense held the potent Bengals in check and Washington has won three of four.
body: LANDOVER, Md. — The Washington Commanders needed a win to keep pace in the NFC East. They not only got a win, their defense made a statement.

The Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on a last-second 28-yard field goal by Drew Stevens to win their second game in a row and third in their last four. It's the first time they've won consecutive games since the 2024 season.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels needed only two passes — 23 yards and 42 yards into tight windows — to lead the Commanders into field goal position. They improved to 4-5-1. A loss would have dropped them three games behind the first-place New York Giants in the NFC East.
Though Daniels led the final drive, it was the defense that kept the Commanders around all night. It held the NFL's hottest offense to only 20 points and continued its improved play.
With a game next week against Arizona, the Commanders have a chance to get to.500.
Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Trend to watch: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned from a groin injury and provided a boost. He carried the ball 13 times for 54 yards and caught two passes for 23 yards. In his previous outing before getting hurt, he gained 82 yards on 11 carries.

Most surprising performance: Washington's defense was outstanding. Joe Burrow entered having completed 21 of his last 22 passes vs. the blitz, but the Commanders never shied from that tactic: He was 8-of-16 for 59 yards Monday.
They also limited receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, holding them to a combined seven catches for 74 yards and a touchdown.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddy Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
The New York Mets continued their spending spree Monday by coming to terms on a one-year deal with first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, a source told ESPN.
Left-handed reliever Brent Suter and the New York Yankees are in agreement on a one-year, $4 million contract with a club option for 2028, sources tell ESPN.
Tarik Skubal and the New York Mets are in agreement on a nine-year, $450 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
The New York Yankees and right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga are in agreement on a two-year deal with a club option for 2029, sources told ESPN, reuniting the reliever and club after a season apart.
Right-hander Troy Melton and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension, sources tell ESPN.
Outfielder Gavin Sheets and the San Diego Padres are in agreement on a three-year, $11 million contract, sources tell ESPN.

The Colorado Rockies are acquiring right-handers Davis Martin and Luis Castillo in a trade with the Chicago White Sox, sources tell ESPN. The White Sox are getting LHP Sean Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz in return.

features.headline: Tarik Skubal free agency tracker: Latest as MLB's top free agent signs with Mets
features.desc: Who will land the two-time Cy Young Award winner? We have all the latest updates on where things stand.
body: And just like that, Tarik Skubal's much-anticipated free agency is over — and in historic fashion.
MLB's top free agent is joining the New York Mets on a record nine-year, $450 million deal, the richest deal ever for a pitcher, both by total value and average annual value ($50 million).
The agreement gives Skubal a home ahead of the impending labor stoppage, as the current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1.
After that, no players can sign until a new CBA is established, which put Skubal on the fast track to a new contract, as many around the sport expect him to sign ahead of the lockout.
We have everything you need to know about Skubal's foray into free agency.

features.headline: Tarik Skubal gives union 450 million more reasons to fight salary cap
features.desc: Baseball's free market isn't perfect, but it allows the best pitcher in the world to get paid what he's worth.
body: Baseball's free-market system is the most honest in North American sports because it offers the fewest restrictions. Free agency really is free.

No salary caps, no boundaries on how much one player can be paid, no artificial limitations on contract length. Just a true accounting of what an athlete's performance is actually worth to the billionaires who decide such things.

For many, it's a harrowing place to be because life on the margins in baseball is brutal. You stick around because maybe you're Jake Bauers and you'll find yourself at 31 guaranteed nearly $60 million on the back of one good season. But mostly it's a grind.

Barely a quarter of players reach the necessary six years of service for free agency because teams control them well beyond those six full big league seasons. It's years in the minor leagues. Options up and down.

For some players, free agency doesn't arrive until a dozen years after they were drafted. Most of that time is spent unable to negotiate their salaries. It is why Major League Baseball players care so much about free agency.
It's not just the spoils or riches. It's that they earned it the honorable way.
All of this animates what happened Sunday afternoon and what's going to be a focus of the next untold number of months in the baseball universe. Tarik Skubal is the best pitcher in the world.

He is also a member of the MLB Players Association's executive subcommittee, a group of eight players that will help guide the union's other 1,192 through the lockout that will formalize baseball's dark winter.

features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
As Paul Goldschmidt has aged out of his peak seasons that culminated with the 2022 National League MVP Award, he has continued to do one thing exceptionally well: mash left-handers.

Over the past two seasons, he has hit.317/.402/.572 against lefties — the fifth-highest OPS among all hitters (Aaron Judge, Shea Langeliers, Coby Mayo and Jackson Chourio are ahead of him, in case you're curious).
Against left-handers, he strikes out just 14.8% of the time, but he hasn't sacrificed power, hitting 18 home runs in 306 at-bats.
Against right-handers, however, he has been useless, putting up backup infielder numbers:.235/.271/.337 with 10 home runs in 528 at-bats.
The Yankees gave him nearly 200 plate appearances against righties in 2026 for some reason, but Goldschmidt should be strictly viewed as a platoon bat at first base or DH.

Certainly, the Mets needed help at first base and/or DH: They were 28th in OPS at first base and 20th at DH. Between the two positions combined, the Mets were 29th in OPS, 29th in RBIs, 29th in batting average and 29th in on-base percentage.
